title: The effect of polyphenols in olive oil on heart disease risk factors: a randomized trial
authors: Covas MI, Nyyssönen K, Poulsen HE, Kaikkonen J, Zunft HJ, Kiesewetter H, et al.
followUp: three 3-week intervention periods, each preceded by a 2-week washout
population: Healthy men at 6 research centres in Spain, Finland, Denmark, Germany and Italy; the registry entry specifies non-smokers aged 20 to 60 years
funder: By grant QLK1-CT-2001-00287 from the Commission of the European Communities Quality of Life and Management of Living Resources program. The registry lists the European Commission as non-commercial sponsor.
authorConflicts: Disclosures: none disclosed. J Kaikkonen and JT Salonen are listed at Oy Jurilab, Kuopio, a Finnish company; Salonen contributed to conception and design and Kaikkonen to analysis and interpretation of the data, and the acknowledgements credit T Vilppo of Oy Jurilab with performing the oxidative and antioxidative biomarker measurements.
result: Randomised crossover trial; 25 mL a day of olive oils with low (2.7 mg/kg), medium (164 mg/kg) or high (366 mg/kg) phenolic content, otherwise similar. HDL cholesterol rose linearly: 0.025 mmol/L (95% CI 0.003 to 0.05), 0.032 mmol/L (0.005 to 0.05) and 0.045 mmol/L (0.02 to 0.06); the total to HDL cholesterol ratio fell linearly with phenolic content; triglycerides fell by an average 0.05 mmol/L with all oils. Oxidised LDL changed by 1.21 U/L (-0.8 to 3.6), -1.48 U/L (-3.6 to 0.6) and -3.21 U/L (-5.1 to -0.8); oxidative stress markers fell linearly with phenolic content. Results read from the abstract; the full text was not accessible.
